lead: Six days before the 4 November municipal elections, Ramaphosa has wrapped up his last eThekwini campaign stop as polls point to an MK lead in Durban. Abroad, the US Fed held rates and Israel's election ended in deadlock.

items.title: Special votes open Monday as IEC readies for 4 November polls
items.summary: About 2.6 million people are expected to cast special ballots on 2 and 3 November, including more than 600,000 home visits. Some 29 million are registered, and the IEC has opened its national results centre in Midrand.

items.title: Polls put MK ahead in eThekwini, but analysts doubt an outright majority
items.summary: Survey estimates for the MK party in Durban range from 33% to 55%, and analyst models land between 40% and 47%. One analyst projects the ANC may lose most or all of its wards in the metro.

items.title: Ramaphosa makes final eThekwini campaign push for the ANC
items.summary: The president spent two days in the metro, including door-to-door visits in eMagabheni, trying to win back voters lost to MK in 2024. The trip comes as soldiers remain in Durban after recent anti-immigrant violence.

items.title: Suliman Carrim granted R100,000 bail but stays behind bars
items.summary: A Pretoria magistrate released the North West businessman on bail in his case over repeated no-shows at the Madlanga Commission, ordering him to appear there within 48 hours. A separate Musina vehicle-theft case keeps him in custody for now.

items.title: Ex-spy tells court SSA operation against the EFF had no security basis
items.summary: In the Pretoria fraud trial of two former State Security Agency officials over about R12 million linked to 2015's Project Mayibuye, a former agent testified the EFF posed no national security threat. The State has closed its case.

items.title: Joburg water protests spread days before the vote
items.summary: Melville residents took to the streets again over supply problems they say have lasted more than eight weeks, with outages also hitting Westdene, the southern suburbs and parts of Lesedi. More protests are planned this week.

items.title: 16 released on warning after violent Samwu protest in Johannesburg
items.summary: The accused face public violence and malicious damage charges after a municipal workers' protest saw roads blocked, tyres burnt and a council truck damaged. The case returns to court on 3 December.

items.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock, with Arab parties holding the balance
items.summary: Exit polls give both Netanyahu's bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition about 51 of 120 seats, short of the 61 needed. Arab lists won around 17-18 seats, and lengthy coalition talks or a minority government are possible.

items.title: US midterms six days out, with Democrats ahead in a key national poll
items.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll puts Democrats at 47% to Republicans' 36% ahead of the 3 November vote, with Trump's approval at 32%. Tight Senate races in Texas, Michigan, Ohio and Kansas are drawing heavy spending.

items.title: Putin courts African leaders at Moscow summit
items.summary: Delegations from 48 African countries, 22 led by heads of state, attended the third Russia-Africa Summit. Putin cast Russia as a non-colonial partner and said it shipped 13 million tonnes of farm produce to Africa this year.

items.title: Houthis claim missile strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they hit a 550,000 barrel-a-day Saudi refinery, which Riyadh had not immediately confirmed. Brent crude climbed above $115 a barrel on the news before easing.

items.title: Cyclone Arnab hits eastern India, killing at least three
items.summary: The very severe cyclonic storm made landfall in Andhra Pradesh with winds of up to 135 km/h. More than 180,000 people were evacuated from Andhra Pradesh and Odisha beforehand.

items.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75-4% as two officials push for a hike
items.summary: The US central bank kept rates on hold in a 10-2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack favouring an increase. It upgraded its view of the economy to strong and will hold fewer policy meetings from 2027.

items.title: Rand trades around R16.6 to the dollar as oil spikes
items.summary: The rand eased early on Wednesday as oil jumped after the Saudi refinery attack and markets waited for the Fed. The 2035 government bond yield rose to 8.6% and the Top 40 slipped in early trade.

items.title: Eskom chair says double-digit tariff hikes are over
items.summary: Mteto Nyati says the Eskom 2.0 plan is on track and future increases should track consumer inflation, after more than 500 days without load shedding and a steep drop in diesel spending.

items.title: Tourist arrivals up 10% this year, Stats SA says
items.summary: International tourist arrivals rose 10.3% from January to September compared with last year, led by Africa and Europe. September saw about 2.88 million cross-border movements.

items.title: Australia edge ahead in Newlands Test decider
items.summary: After the Proteas were bowled out for 329, Australia closed day two on 330 for 4, with Josh Inglis on 85 not out. Marco Jansen took his 100th Test wicket. The series is level at 1-1.

items.title: Erasmus names six uncapped players in 37-man Bok squad for Europe
items.summary: Etzebeth, Kolbe, Esterhuizen and Pollard are out injured. The Springboks face Italy in Genoa on 7 November, then France and Ireland, before finals weekend in London.

items.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 on penalties in the Carabao Cup
items.summary: The tie finished 1-1 with both goals from the spot, Morgan Rogers for Chelsea and Cody Gakpo for Liverpool. Wesley Fofana's miss in the shootout sent Liverpool into the quarter-finals.

items.title: Microsoft and Alphabet post big cloud gains as AI spending soars
items.summary: Azure grew 48% and Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion. Alphabet's quarterly capex reached $51.4 billion, turning its free cash flow negative, and it expects spending to rise sharply again in 2027.

items.title: Labour Court voids CCMA ruling that cited a fake, AI-made case
items.summary: A judge found a CCMA commissioner relied on a non-existent Constitutional Court judgment in a Post Office dismissal dispute, apparently from AI, and called it a fundamental failure of justice.
